claim: UNKNOWN: whether Freesound holds any Moogerfooger recording. The Freesound search page could not be opened (web-fetch allowlist refusal and a 403 from the egress proxy), and search-engine queries restricted to freesound.org returned no sound tagged or titled Moogerfooger (only unrelated Moog synth packs and a DIY LM13700 ring-modulator session).

Freesound's FAQ states three licences are offered to uploaders (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-NC) and that a registered, logged-in account is needed to download a sound; the FAQ is silent on scripted or bulk download.

UNKNOWN: whether Wikimedia Commons has Moogerfooger audio. A search-engine snapshot lists a Category:Moogerfooger page, but fetching it returned page-not-found and the Commons API was blocked (403), so its contents are unverified; the English Wikipedia Moogerfooger article embeds no audio and links no Commons audio.

A query of the Zenodo records API for the text moogerfooger returned zero records overall, and the same word (plus Moog, Moog pedal, analog delay pedal, ring modulator pedal) restricted to audio-type open records also returned zero, so Zenodo holds no record that names a Moogerfooger in its indexed metadata.

Zenodo's Terms of Use v1.3 say downloading content means accepting the terms, access is for non-military purposes, no intellectual property passes to the downloader, and the downloader must obey each record's licence; the terms set no explicit rule on automated or API access.

The Internet Archive Access Policy defers use of its collection to a separate Terms of Use page (archive.org/about/terms.php); that page could not be opened in this session (allowlist refusal), so the archive.org terms on personal or automated download are UNKNOWN here.

EGFxSet (Zenodo 7044411, CC BY 4.0, 5.8 GB, creators Pedroza, Meza and Roman) contains a clean guitar set plus 12 real-hardware effects (Boss BD-2, Ibanez Mini Tube Screamer, Pro Co RAT2, Boss CE-3, Mooer E-Lady, MXR Phase 45, Line 6 DL4 in three modes, Orange CR-60 reverbs) and no Moogerfooger.

Kent and John Blackford), and Vol. 3 (2010-12-03) track 13 lists an unspecified Moogerfooger Analog Delay (The Vegan Surgeons); MP3 only, no settings, no dry counterpart; no-derivatives terms make them personal-listening material only.

claim: A GitHub repository search for moogerfooger returned 9 repositories; 6 were cloned and inspected (nstilt1/mofo-repo, ozpv/mf-102, alessandro-scalambrino/MoogerFooger-Emulation, europa78/MOOGERFOOGER-PEDAL-WAVEFORM-EDITOR-, brunomorgado/moogerfooger, henriksvensson/moogerfoogerdooger) and none contains a Moogerfooger audio recording, impulse response or frequency-response measurement (they are source code; the MF-104M emulation is MIT-licensed code with a copy of the manual PDF; mofo-repo is an unlicensed envelope-filter VST). The other 3 (pjm-moogerfooger, pmuellrgitoff/pjm-moogerfooger, SVG-Effects-Pedals tribute pack) were not opened and are, by their descriptions, Max for Live wrappers and fan art.

No openly licensed frequency-response plot, impulse response or other measurement of any Moogerfooger pedal was found in Zenodo, the inspected GitHub repositories, or the pages above; DAFx 'Practical Modeling of Bucket-Brigade Device Circuits' and a Padua thesis by R. Simionato surfaced in search as possible sources of BBD-delay measurements but were NOT opened, and the Moog hardware manuals were not read for specification tables, so those leads remain UNKNOWN.

MF-101 Lowpass Filter: 0 redistributable (CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA) recordings found; 1 restrictive-but-personally-usable item (the TONE3000 drive-stage NAM capture, a model not a recording); 0 dry/wet pairs; coverage gaps: Freesound, Commons, SoundCloud and YouTube could not be searched or opened.
